checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are highly accurate and rigorous. It correctly identified that while the global silhouette (rectangular prism) matches, the critical functional components (spools, head slot, molded details) are completely absent, being merely 2D illustrations on a solid surface. The Router was not lenient; it correctly marked 'is_present: false' for all internal/functional checkpoints. The distinction between a 'cassette' and a 'luggage tag with a cassette drawing' is the key failure mode here, which the Router captured perfectly.
artifact_review: The Router's identification of 'structural_collapse' (Severity 4) is appropriate because the object fails to be a cassette in any functional or structural sense—it is a flat slab. The 'text_gibberish' (Severity 2) is also correctly identified; the text auditor confirmed no legible text exists, only hallucinated strokes. The 'perspective_distortion' of the strap (Severity 1) is a minor but valid observation of physical implausibility. I agree with all severities; the structural failure is the dominant artifact.
alignment_reasoning: Only 2 out of 9 checkpoints passed (global shape and corner rounding). The Fine Grained Classifier was fooled by the visual similarity (Top-1: cassette), but this is a false positive due to the lack of structural depth verified by the Geometry checkpoints. The image depicts an illustration of a cassette on a tag, not a cassette itself. This represents a severe semantic and structural misalignment with the class definition.
artifact_reasoning: The primary artifact is the complete lack of internal structure (spools, tape, slots), reducing the object to a 2D print on a 3D slab (Structural Collapse). Text generation failed completely (gibberish/unreadable). The strap attachment is physically ambiguous. These are significant generative failures that prevent the object from being recognized as a real-world instance of the class.
key_defects: Functional components are 2D illustrations rather than 3D structures
